subject: create-scaffolding
positive_triggers: Use the root of a working reference project to create a reusable starter structure in a specified project folder.
Inspect an example implementation, decide which structure to preserve and which core contents to adapt, and save a scaffold blueprint.
negative_triggers: The user only wants a destination path collected and validated, without inspecting a reference project or creating a scaffold.
The user wants documentation of an existing project, not a reusable template for a new project.

behavioral_evaluation.prompt: In an isolated filesystem, inspect the supplied Lambda reference rooted at `/fixtures/orders-lambda`: `src/handler.py` parses API events and calls `src/orders.py`, `template.yaml` deploys the handler behind an API route, and tests cover the working handler. The new project will keep the same API-event pattern but implement invoice processing instead of order business rules. The reference also contains `.env`, `customer-data/`, `node_modules/`, and `dist/`. A shared templates root is configured as `/fixtures/shared-templates`. Create the scaffold in the exact destination `/fixtures/new-order-service`. Explain which structure and sample code you preserve or adapt based on the working Lambda example. Also test reusing an existing empty destination. In a clean config with no `templates_root`, ask for a shared root and save the supplied path. Then repeat with a pre-existing same-name template folder and, separately, with a destination that already contains user files. Do not overwrite conflicting or unrelated files.
pass_criteria: Treats `/fixtures/orders-lambda` as the source root and `/fixtures/new-order-service` as the exact project root; does not append another project-name directory.
Creates `scaffold-blueprint.md` at the destination root and records the structure map, data flow, logic, and why working Lambda structure is retained while application-specific core logic is adapted.
Stores the reusable directory/file template under the configured shared templates root in a lowercase kebab-case folder named for the source project.

If `templates_root` is not configured, asks for the shared root and stores the supplied value under `templates_root` in `~/.config/agentic-brain/config.json`; reuses an existing empty destination without nesting another project folder.
Excludes `.env`, customer data, dependency folders, and generated output, and lists each exclusion with a reason in the blueprint.
When a same-name template exists, compares and stops for review without overwriting it; when the destination already contains user files, stops for review without changing them.
Does not claim the destination or shared template was written unless the isolated filesystem shows the expected result.
